timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only mirrored stream; no semantic events were projected, but all lines are accounted for in the manifest.
Parent probed PyYAML behavior, wrote contract and pyvalues, launched the workflow, expanded corpora while children ran, waited in long sleeps, and ended with exit 137.
Repr and argparse child read the shared contract/value model, wrote pyrepr and argparse modules, tested edge cases, and returned a completed report.
YAML front-half child read the contract/value model, wrote nodes/events/resolver/representer/serializer/dumper modules, tested components, and returned a completed report.
One emitter retry read shared inputs and existing files but was interrupted before producing the required emitter implementation.
Another emitter retry read the same starting context, probed only minimal behavior, and was interrupted without returning a usable result.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the main requirements: pure ESM Node.js, .mjs files, manual argparse-compatible --a parsing, no npm dependencies, no Python calls, no JSON/RegExp, and byte-aligned PyYAML output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent built a shared contract/value model, then delegated five module groups in one workflow: repr/argparse, tokenizer/parser, evaluator, YAML front half, and emitter. Integration and differential testing were scheduled only after all build agents returned.
parallel.implementation: Parent produced CONTRACT.md and pyvalues.mjs. Three child lines completed useful libraries, but evaluator and emitter work repeatedly stalled, and no integrated evaluator/emitter/entry-point candidate was returned to the parent.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The workflow planned an integration child to write test2.mjs after build completion, but the build never completed. Artifact validation found only library files and no expected test2.mjs entry point.
parallel.verification: Parent verified isolated pyFloatRepr/base64 and resolver behavior while children ran, but no end-to-end node /output/test2.mjs check or whole artifact differential test occurred because no entry point existed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with workflow status killed, no aggregate workflow result, no integration phase, no test2.mjs, and an official completed retry result of 0/131.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same migration requirements and directly probed many PyYAML, argparse, Python eval, formatting, escaping, and YAML resolver cases before coding.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, integration, testing, and delivery in one workspace, with no delegation or child handoff boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote a complete module tree including Python value/eval helpers, YAML emitter/dump modules, CLI parsing, and /output/test2.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run explicitly wrote the entry point, ran it on a sample case, and artifact validation found test2.mjs plus supporting library and test files.
serial.verification: It ran a local 198-case differential test to completion and launched a much larger generated corpus; official evaluation later completed with 25/131 passed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out during the larger background corpus and did not fully match the evaluator, but it delivered a runnable artifact with partial official success.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full ESM/no-dependency/no-Python/manual-CLI/PyYAML byte-parity obligation and encoded it into its workflow contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and kept them in one continuous implementation context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was similar; the material difference was downstream execution, because serial carried the recognized requirements into a delivered entry point while parallel did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated five build module groups and made integration conditional on all child build reports returning.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept implementation, integration, and verification under one actor that could change any module and the entry point as needed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more component owners but placed the critical entry-point owner after a workflow join; serial had a single owner and reached the entry-point write.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied detailed child briefs with shared AST/interface contracts and read-before-write rules, so missing task or interface context is not the main failure boundary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained interface decisions within one trajectory and wrote compatible imports across its modules and test2.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's context transfer was comparatively explicit, but the workflow could not consume all child work into an integrated artifact; serial avoided cross-agent handoff risk by retaining local context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a shared value model and several library modules, but evaluator/emitter completion and the entry point were absent at artifact capture.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a broad module tree and the entry test file, including CLI, Python expression evaluation, YAML emission, and local tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial delivered a runnable implementation path; parallel delivered only partial components because the workflow never reached integration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Some child results completed, but the aggregate workflow result remained null and the workflow status was killed after stall retries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle and consumed its own local edits immediately, including writing and executing the entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's dependent integration was blocked by unfinished child lifecycle; serial had no join barrier before packaging.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote into shared /output, but final artifact validation showed only partial library files and no assembled test2.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and packaged a coherent output tree with test2.mjs and library/test support files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The decisive integration difference is the missing parallel entry point versus the serial artifact that included one.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran isolated checks for pyFloatRepr/base64 and resolver only; no integrated test2.mjs check or full differential suite occurred.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial executed test2.mjs on the sample and then reached a 198/198 local differential suite before timing out on a larger generated corpus.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had end-to-end local acceptance evidence before closure; parallel had only component checks and then an official 0/131 result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent most of the remaining run in a workflow whose emitter/evaluator children stalled and retried until the final wait ended with exit 137.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but after creating the artifact, passing its local 198-case suite, and launching a larger background corpus.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The same global budget closure hit very different artifact states: parallel before assembly, serial after a runnable partial solution.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed status records make this a both_fail pair: parallel passed 0/131 and serial passed 25/131. The quality gap is concrete. Parallel delegated the main implementation to a workflow that never completed its build join or integration phase, so the artifact lacked test2.mjs. Serial timed out too, but only after writing the entry point, testing it locally, and packaging a runnable output tree.
parallel_contributors: Workflow fan-out plus repeated stall retries consumed the remaining run window before the integration child could write test2.mjs.
Parallel verification stayed at component-level checks because the integrated entry point never existed.
serial_contributors: Serial kept ownership of implementation and integration in one trajectory and wrote /output/test2.mjs.
Serial completed a 198-case local differential suite before launching a larger background corpus that was killed at timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial still failed most hidden official cases, so it had substantive implementation gaps unrelated to concurrency.
Parallel may have had ordinary component defects in partial modules, but the official 0/131 result is already explained by the missing entry artifact.
evaluator_effects: Parallel cell/evaluation/summary.json is a stale incomplete first evaluator attempt; cell/status.json contains the completed official retry used for this outcome.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors for the quality gap, not an exclusive root cause and not a discordant pass/fail outcome

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was assigned to the workflow children and parent, even though some child work stalled.
The workflow explicitly created an integration agent after the build phase; the issue was that the join never reached it.
The integration assignment owned the final entry point and assembly, so the missing test2.mjs resulted from nonarrival, not owner omission.
The workflow script owned the build-to-integrate-to-difftest pipeline; it failed under stalled children rather than absent pipeline ownership.
The parent did serial probing and contract writing before launch, but the retained adverse episode is the later workflow fan-out and retry exhaustion.
The investigation did not remain a pure investigator phase; the parent also wrote the shared implementation foundation before launching build children.
The critical path was delayed by collective child breadth and repeated retries, making Fan-out Budget Exhaustion the more specific load pattern.
Five workflow build agents plus repeated stalled retry attempts consumed the finite run window; the workflow was killed before integration and the artifact had no expected entry point.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel artifact omitted test2.mjs and reached the official evaluator with only partial libraries, producing 0/131 where serial's delivered artifact passed 25/131.
candidates.near_match_reason: Emitter and evaluator subtasks were large, but the observed failure chain was collective fan-out plus retry exhaustion across multiple children rather than one isolated oversized child.

candidates.reason: The emitter and evaluator scopes were large, but the adverse chain combined multiple stalled children and repeated retries, so the retained label is Fan-out Budget Exhaustion.
Executed children were given the task, hard rules, file targets, and acceptance probes; no known requirement disappeared from a child brief and caused unusable work.
The workflow brief specified exact exports, AST node shapes, event classes, file names, and import expectations; incompatibility was not observed because integration never ran.
There is no evidence that known task findings were omitted or truncated during a transfer and then caused repeated or wrong work.
Some reports and specs were lengthy, but the receiver never reached integration; no available bulky handoff was shown to be unconsumable at a decision point.
No child or parent is shown acting on a superseded workspace state or outdated requirement after newer state was observable.
Completed child reports did not present incompatible contracts that reached the parent and remained unadjudicated before a wrong integration step.
Parallel made no observable whole-task completion decision; it timed out with an empty final response and missing entry point.
The workflow retried stalled children, but repeated work is counted inside the fan-out budget episode rather than as a separately proven checkpoint-free retry.

candidates.reason: Several child attempts were interrupted by stall retry or timeout, but those are the terminal symptoms of the same fan-out budget chain.
There was no complete promotable candidate or compatible component set ready for final placement; critical evaluator/emitter/entry pieces were incomplete.
No child implementation was merged after an integrated verification step; the integrated verification step never occurred.
Some partial child modules were available, but there was no completed delegated implementation ready to join into a final executable artifact.
No verifier child produced a trapped concrete finding; the missing aggregate result came from the stalled build workflow.
The parent was killed while waiting for the workflow; lack of takeover is not separated from the retained fan-out/retry budget exhaustion chain.
Completed child results were not ignored in favor of a conflicting action; the workflow join stayed blocked by unfinished required children.
The parent periodically checked output files, journal state, and component tests before the final wait; the adverse episode is retry exhaustion, not total absence of inspection.
Children owned adjacent modules, but no competing cross-file design collision reached an observed reconciliation failure.
No live agents are shown editing the same source file and then observing or reconciling the concurrent change.
No non-entry source produced or actively owned by one agent was wholesale replaced by another with a proven adverse effect.
The required deliverable test2.mjs was never created in parallel, so there was no entry-point overwrite event.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing another agent's final-tree work.
Agents wrote a shared /output workspace, but the observed problem was incomplete workflow completion, not unstable provenance from unisolated writes.
No actor consumed another actor's temporary file, cache, fixture, or generated artifact as a contaminated reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel workflow required all five module build children to finish before starting integration, then retried stalled critical children until the workflow was killed. That consumed the available budget and left no test2.mjs deliverable.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel artifact omitted test2.mjs and reached the official evaluator with only partial libraries, producing 0/131 where serial's delivered artifact passed 25/131.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Emitter and evaluator subtasks were large, but the evidence shows a collective workflow fan-out and retry budget drain across multiple children, so one child-scope label would be narrower than the actual episode.

deduplicated_same_label_episodes: Multiple emitter and evaluator retry attempts are treated as one fan-out budget episode.
suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Oversized Child Task, Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, Missing Implementation Join, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered but rejected as same-chain or less direct descriptions of the stalled workflow.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were reviewed; no other independent coordination consequence was directly evidenced.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Only the collective fan-out budget episode is retained; downstream missing entry, killed wait, and stalled children are not split into extra labels.
